cross_market_insights: Every market shows an AI Overview first, then a weak organic set: Pinterest pins, a Reddit thread, an Instagram profile, a ceremony-tool blog and small US officiant or elopement-planner sites. No major publisher and no Australian editorial page ranks top 3.

No top-3 result (from snippets) gives the Australian legal wording (the s 45 vow words and the monitum), the NOIM timing or the two-witness rule, and none separates a legal elopement at home from a symbolic ceremony abroad. That is the gap.
Two of the twelve top-3 slots are intent mismatches (how to tell family you are eloping). Searchers also want short, copyable scripts: related searches add 'pdf', 'short' and 'funny'.
PAA repeats 'What does the officiant say at a wedding before the vows?' in all four markets: answer it directly in the script section.

London's SERP leans to officiant script pages and announcement scripts; the AU SERPs lean to Pinterest. A clean, word-for-word, two-person script with legal and symbolic variants marked inline has no real competitor in any market.
Nobody covers setting and timing for a destination elopement (light, wind and sound, permits, a wet-weather fallback, how long the script runs). That is the destination edge the user asked for.
payload.recommended_angle: The only elopement ceremony script written for two people, word for word, with every line marked as needed for a legal Australian elopement or swappable for a symbolic ceremony abroad, plus the timing and setting notes a destination elopement actually needs. Shows the invisible work (NOIM lead time, witnesses, signing, permits, light and wet-weather plans) without selling a big wedding.
